I’m a firm believer that the best brand campaigns don’t just tell people what a company does, they remind people why it matters. That belief is at the heart of Power of Belief, our new campaign at [Kickstarter](https://www.linkedin.com/company/kickstarter?trk=public_profile__posts-text). Over the past several months, I’ve had the privilege of working alongside an incredibly talented team to bring this idea to life. It was inspired by a simple truth: when people believe in original ideas, and in the people bold enough to pursue them, culture moves forward. Every day, creators take that leap on [Kickstarter](https://www.linkedin.com/company/kickstarter?trk=public_profile__posts-text), and every day, backers who support them by helping turn those ideas into reality. This campaign is about celebrating that belief. Not just belief in creativity, but belief in each other and in what’s possible when a community comes together to support something new. Watching this come to life has been one of the most meaningful moments of my time at [Kickstarter](https://www.linkedin.com/company/kickstarter?trk=public_profile__posts-text) , and we’re just getting started. I can’t wait to share what’s next. Two conferences in a day. Lots of ideas. Started in heels, ended in flats. A few takeaways from SoComm and the Female Quotient AI Summit. Different conversations, but reinforcing reminders about the power of brand, personalization and creativity. → What your brand stands for matters more than ever. Adobe’s [Loni](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lonistark?trk=public_profile__reactions-text) (who was hilarious on stage) got right to it: “Don't lose what your brand stands for with all this shiny technology. Give your customers and consumers something to be loyal for.” As AI, automated content and agentic solutions accelerate, people will always need something to believe in. Technology creates convenience. Brand creates connection. → Your next customer might not be human. The idea of a personal agent becoming an “extended member of your customer's family” was a great (and maybe jarring) visual. I imagined one sitting at the Thanksgiving table! As agents increasingly help people search, compare and buy, brands will have two storefronts: one that builds an emotional connection with people, and another that makes the brand discoverable to machines. → Knowing your audience is one thing. Knowing what matters to them is another. “People are expecting to be known and not sorted.” Loved this framing from [Nicole](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nicoleturner17?trk=public_profile__reactions-text) at Merge. How do we use the tools available to build better relationships, not just more sophisticated segments? And as [Josh](https://www.linkedin.com/in/joshua-blyskal?trk=public_profile__reactions-text) put it, “It's really easy now to create things, but it's really hard to know what exactly to create.” As production gets easier, judgment and taste become even more valuable. → Creator commerce is growing up. Brand-side operating models need to catch up. [Jamie](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jamiegutfreund?trk=public_profile__reactions-text) highlighted how creator marketing is often spread across five to eight teams, each with different budgets, KPIs and measurement. The data is just as fragmented, making it hard to see what's working and where to invest. Meanwhile, [Lauren](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lauren-inganamort-77674442?trk=public_profile__reactions-text) shared that LTK has cultivated nearly 500 millionaires, adding one per week over the last 18 months. Wild. And a final reminder from [John](https://www.linkedin.com/in/johnkraski?trk=public_profile__reactions-text) on the power of failure: “There's more things that fail behind the scenes than are actually successful. The reality is, 95% of the stuff we're doing is probably failure. We're iterating to get it to where it needs to be to be successful.” A good reminder that the polished result rarely tells the whole story. So much fun spending the day with some of my besties and new friends: [Colin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/colin-duethorn?trk=public_profile__reactions-text), [John](https://www.linkedin.com/in/johnkraski?trk=public_profile__reactions-text), [Whitney](https://www.linkedin.com/in/whitney-carmichael-962b62256?trk=public_profile__reactions-text), [Laura](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nardellal?trk=public_profile__reactions-text) and [Ted](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ted-merz-cfa-b711257?trk=public_profile__reactions-text). And especially [Jamie](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jamiegutfreund?trk=public_profile__reactions-text), for the best subway ride + lunch I've had in a while! Didn't get to hang with [Martha Stewart](https://www.linkedin.com/in/marthakstewart?trk=public_profile__reactions-text), but I wish I had. Legendary. ❤️
